newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed in range-bound trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday as April failed to break out of its recent boundaries amid talk of steady cash, industry sources said.

April settled 0.4 cent lower at $1.892 per mmBtu after trading in only a five-cent range and failing to break through a low of $1.87 and a high of $1.92. May finished up 0.1 cent at $1.947, while other deferreds were mostly higher.
"Cash and futures have been running neck and neck. Unless cash makes a big move, I don't see it (April) breaking out of this range tomorrow," one trader said.

Technically, traders were still looking for a retest of $1.85. Further support was seen at the March 3 low of $1.78 and then at $1.701 contract low. After today's high of $1.92, April resistance was pegged at $2 and the mid-teens.
Ahead of April's expiry on Monday, traders are pegging May support at $1.90 and $1.845 and resistance at $1.99 and $2.04.
April Hub gas options expire Friday, while April futures expire Monday.

Cash prices continued to mimick futures today as prices at Henry Hub, La., stood at $1.86-1.89. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes were also steady in the low-to-mid $1.70s, with Demarcation quoted around $1.75. At the New York city-gate, prices were about five cents lower in the low-to-mid $2.20s.

Also helping to keep the market steady was American Gas Association storage data, showing a drop of 45 bcf in the U.S. last week to 886 bcf, which was in line with expectations and 218 bcf ahead of year-ago.
Inventories in the West dropped two bcf to 163 bcf, down 319 from year-ago levels. In the East, stocks were down 57 bcf to 469 bcf, while producing region inventories gained 14 bcf to 254 bcf.
No NYMEX Permian or Alberta contracts traded.

KCBT's April contract, which expires Tuesday, ended unchanged at $1.70, still even with current cash values. Deferreds were a half-cent to one cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.2 cent to 19.2 cents (NYMEX premium).
Permian basin cash prices edged about two cents higher to the high-$1.60s to mid-$1.70s, as above-normal temperatures blanketed the Southwest.
